label: original-phase input of o/a/k/p (weaker u/f/n/v/d), early in sequence
explanation: Input-driven unit that fires almost only in the original phase (99% of mass); it is essentially silent at <DEL> and during copy. It fires most on the input tokens o, a, k, p (each about 27% firing rate, 5x lift, about 68% of mass together). u, f, n, v, d give weaker firing (adding them raises mass recall to 0.94 but halves precision). Firing rate falls steadily with position (13% at t=0-1, under 3% by t>=7) and is much lower on repeated tokens (in_first=0: 0.9% rate). The strongest examples come after sequences that start with y/i/l. Even on its preferred tokens it fires only about half the time, depending on history in ways that position, first occurrence, previous token, and prefix-set conditions do not capture (none got dev F1 above 0.555). It does not fire on output/copy steps or on tokens like j, s, r, digits.
